{{recipe}}

'''Iraqi charoset''' is a dried fruit and nut-based paste served during the Jewish celebration of Passover by Jews from Iraq.

==Ingredients==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]] Iraqi [[cookbook:date|date]]s, [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] and seeded
* [[Cookbook:Water|Water]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]]
* 125 ml chopped [[cookbook:walnut|walnut]]s or [[cookbook:pistachio|pistachio]]s

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] dates in lightly salted water stirring frequently until it is a thick paste.
# Mix in finely chopped nuts.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* A traditional variant is made by straining the pulp out of the paste producing a honey-like date [[Cookbook:Syrup|syrup]]. This procedure uses considerably more dates and can take several days to produce sufficient syrup.
